_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); revenue, margin, expense and receivables signals with Google's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Alphabet is a collection of businesses — the largest of which is Google.' 'We generate a significant portion of our revenues from advertising, and reduced spending by advertisers, a loss of partners, or new and existing technologies that block ads online and/or affect our ability to customize ads could harm our business.' 'We face intense competition.' 'Our operating results have fluctuated, and may in the future fluctuate, as a result of a number of factors, many outside of our control, including the cyclicality and seasonality in our business and geopolitical events.' 'In addition, expenditures by advertisers tend to be cyclical, reflecting overall economic conditions and budgeting and buying patterns.' (FY2021 10-K); CYCLICAL: the 10-K says so of its own business ('the cyclicality and seasonality in our business'), the BKR, CAT and NVDA reading, not an industry's words; CLOUD (live from 2012-10-30) is scoped to public cloud displacing on-premise IT, and this 10-K names the cloud as Google's own business ('Within Google Cloud, we devote significant resources to develop and deploy our enterprise-ready cloud services, including Google Cloud Platform and Google Workspace') and enterprise cloud providers as its competitors, so it is out of scope (the AVGO FY2012 and NVDA reading); ECOMMERCE (from 2015-01-01), STREAMING (from 2015-08-04) and ENERGY_TRANSITION (from 2015-12-12) are scoped to physical retail, linear TV and pay-TV bundles, and fossil fuels; EV (from 2020-01-01) to combustion-engine vehicles and their suppliers; CRYPTO (from 2020-10-21) to payment networks, banks and exchanges; no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a search and advertising company on the 10-K's date, so the watch list is empty; the 10-K names AI only as Google's own products and their challenges ('new and evolving products and services, including those that use AI and machine learning, raise ethical, technological, legal, regulatory, and other challenges, which may negatively affect our brands and demand for our products and services.'); the competition named is a competitive field, not a theme, and stays here (the PEP obesity rule)

(FY2021 10-K); CYCLICAL: the 10-K says so of its own business ('the cyclicality and seasonality in our business'), the BKR, CAT and NVDA reading, not an industry's words; CLOUD (live from 2012-10-30) is scoped to public cloud displacing on-premise IT, and this 10-K names the cloud as Google's own business ('Within Google Cloud, we devote significant resources to develop and deploy our enterprise-ready cloud services, including Google Cloud Platform and Google Workspace') and enterprise cloud providers as its competitors, so it is out of scope (the AVGO FY2012 and NVDA reading); ECOMMERCE (from 2015-01-01), STREAMING (from 2015-08-04) and ENERGY_TRANSITION (from 2015-12-12) are scoped to physical retail, linear TV and pay-TV bundles, and fossil fuels; EV (from 2020-01-01) to combustion-engine vehicles and their suppliers; CRYPTO (from 2020-10-21) to payment networks, banks and exchanges; no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a search and advertising company on the 10-K's date, so the watch list is empty; the 10-K names AI only as Google's own products and their challenges ('new and evolving products and services, including those that use AI and machine learning, raise ethical, technological, legal, regulatory, and other challenges, which may negatively affect our brands and demand for our products and services.'); the competition named is a competitive field, not a theme, and stays here (the PEP obesity rule). cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.53x; +0% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.64; conservative 2yr +81%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -35.4%/yr (worst year FY12-FY21, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +22.8%/yr (Q1 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +23.2%/yr (FY12-FY21 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +65.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY12-FY21, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: GOOG (retrospective, 2022-07-15) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.53x (57.6% downside to Bear $956.15 / +108.3% upside to Bull $4697.24) | Adj composite 2.25 vs market 1.61: gap +0.64 [UNDERVALUED] | +1% above the EPP floor $2,244.00 (20x FY22E $112.20) | Conservative 2-yr case: +81.4% total (+40.7%/yr) | At 20.1x FY22E the 15% hurdle price $2,982.69 sits at or below the BASE case; revenue +23.0% YoY in Q1 2022, forward revenues +23% (Q1 2022 revenue growth (no Q2 2022 guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
